title: Cenotes Dos Ojos, Xel-Ha (J. G. Coke IV 1986)
credits: Cenotes Dos Ojos, Xel-Ha, Quintana Roo; compass & line survey, 1 July 1986, by James Coke, Johanna deGroot; length 958.6 m; drafted JGC/TTS; (c) 1986 James Guthrie Coke IV (AMCS Activities Newsletter no. 16)

scaleBar.why: 0-30-60 meters; not used (no "north"): 0.0837 m/px, 14% more than the fit's 0.0735 (the ponds 162 m apart by the bar, 143 m on the satellite)

placementWhy: Fair (about 10-20 m): free similarity fit on the two ponds, each on the bright-green canopy patch of its sinkhole on the satellite imagery (Bing and Mapbox; the ponds themselves are hidden under the trees): Ojo East on the patch carrying OpenStreetMap's '1st Eye' node (6104810812), Ojo West on the triangular patch 143 m WNW carrying its '2nd Eye' (node 6104810802). Two points fit exactly, so the checks are: the map's north arrow - drawn in Coke's style, its half-barbed end (towards the bottom right) is north, the 'N' standing at its tail, as on his 1987 Naharon map; the hand-drawn twin's arrowhead points the same way, and the twin's 'Xel-Ha 2.5 Km' arrow points along the jeep road to the ESE - is 5.3 degrees from the fit's north (magnetic, 1986); the map's 'East' pond comes out east and 'West' west; both OSM eye nodes fall on their pond outlines' edges; the pond outlines sit on the two canopy patches; the footpath's 'jeep road' is today's access track from Highway 307 (OSM way 59136197) - parallel within 1 degree (bearing 294 on both) and the footpath's end 27 m from where OSM's footpath to the eyes (way 83855802) leaves it at the Dos Ojos parking. Scale: the fit is 12% under the 60 m scale bar; the map's own penetrations don't settle it (p.465m - p.349m = 116 m along the passage: 104 m at the fit, 118 m at the bar; p.507.5m - p.349m = 158.5 m: 164 m at the fit, 187 m at the bar; p.158.5m from Ojo East: 150 m at the fit, 171 m at the bar), while the footpath's length to the road (153 m at the fit, 176 m on the ground) agrees better with the bar: the scale may be up to ~10% low, which would move the far ends of the west passages by up to 20-25 m. The database's Dos Ojos East and West (Google Maps positions) lie 74 m W and 77 m S of the ponds. Cross-checked loosely with the QRSS 1996 line plot (dos-ojos-qrss-1996.json, ~20 m accurate here): its lines around the eyes and west toward Taak Bi Ha run in the same corridor; the ADC sketch (dos-ojos-part.json) is too coarse here.

symbols.why: NSS Cave Diving Section symbols (the map's legend: p = penetration, R minor and X major restriction, S silt, Z zero visibility); depths in metres, underlined (the hand-drawn twin 'Dos Ojos, Cenotes, Xel-Ha' says 'Floor depths in Feet' for its own numbers). All depths but one are single digits, which OCR doesn't take: they are added by hand. Three numbers lack their underline on this drafted copy but are underlined depths on the twin (2 by Ojo East = twin 5'; the two 10s of the north-east loop = twin 30' and 20'): kept as depths with the drafted value. Circled numbers (8, 7; twin 25') are ceiling heights. Twelve wavy flow arrows, bearings from the map's up (the water runs towards Ojo East and on east). No bones: no bones symbol in the legend, no bone shapes in the passages (the rocks are plain ovals, the four star shapes by Ojo West are speleothems - drawn as rocks on the twin), no 'bones' in the text. The passage ends trail off in dashed lines (unsurveyed continuations), without a written pointer.
